profile.headline: Entrepreneurship | Solar | Energy Storage | Software | Education | Community
profile.summary:
I am passionate about innovative technologies that can transform our lives for the better, especially in the areas of education, clean energy, circularity and sustainability.

In addition to building a few moderately successful small businesses, I have also had the *privilege* to fail - a lot.

positions.title: Founder, Software Engineer
positions.description: An education platform for solar and energy storage professionals to earn training, credentials and certification. My partner and co-owner Alex Jarvis is an IREC Certified Master Trainer and Solar PV instructor. I run operations and software development while partnering with experts in the industry to help the solar workforce own their energy future.
positions.insights: Skills: Bootstrap Startup · Sustainability · Education Technology · Artificial Intelligence (AI) · Large Language Models (LLM) · Self-capitalized Startups · Ruby · Software Development · Benefit Companies · Solar Energy · Solar PV · NABCEP

positions.title: Oregon Community Liaison
positions.description:
I lead entrepreneurship and workforce development for the Collaborative: pursuing and managing grant funding, building training and career resources, and running the programming that connects workers, employers, educators, investors, and policymakers across Oregon and Washington.

I also act as the Collaborative's Oregon Liaison hosting: public events, technical workshops, investor roundtables, and community forums that put scientists, engineers, entrepreneurs, and policymakers in the same room. 1,400+ attendees across 17+ events region-wide since 2024.

The Pacific Northwest Battery Collaborative (PNWBC) unites the regional community of workers, builders, and thinkers to create the world’s leading hub for energy storage innovation.
positions.insights: Skills: Lithium-ion Batteries · Solar Energy · Energy Storage · Event Planning · Investing · Process Automation · Community Building · Venture Capital · Event Management · Strategic Planning · Communication · Renewable Energy

positions.title: E8 Oregon Hub Ambassador
positions.description: As an E8 Oregon Hub Ambassador I act as a connector between the Oregon and Washington cleantech investor communities. I help the E8 team to identify, promote and host events in Oregon and Southwest Washington for investors and entrepreneurs focused on environmental impact.

positions.title: Limited Partner - Regener8 Fund I
positions.description:
E8 encourages Cleantech ventures in the US and Canada that are actively seeking Seed to Series A funding. We are on the lookout for strong teams with innovative solutions addressing environmentally important areas such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, energy storage, sustainable transportation, the built environment, water quality, and agtech. 

I am an active investor at E8 and participate in pitch screening and due diligence teams. I invest (small checks) both directly in startups after their diligence phase and also through the Regener8 fund, a member-driven fund which tracks investments of the E8 Angel group.

positions.title: Decarbon8 Screening Committee - Due Diligence Team Lead
positions.description:
I led a Due Diligence team analyzing Gaia AI, one of the four finalists in Decarbon8 2025. Gaia AI is focused on forest data collection and analysis using AI-powered tools and sensor technology. Our report recommended investment in Gaia.

Decarbon8-US is a philanthropic impact fund administered by Realize Impact and E8 Angels. The fund channels personal and philanthropic donations to empower early-stage companies whose technologies and business models accelerate the transition to environmentally sustainable solutions.

The 2025 Decarbon8-US Fund is invested in Software and AI solutions driving climate innovation and decarbonization. The 2025 theme emphasizes capital-light AI and/or software-based innovations focused on making a significant positive impact on climate.

positions.title: Limited Partner
positions.description:
The Intrepid Oregon Fund (IOF) is anchored by a $4 million initial investment by Business Oregon through its Commercialization Gap Fund program. IOF invests in early-stage companies less than five years old, in sectors that are primarily technology and science-focused such as digital health, healthcare IT, bioscience, medical devices, climate-tech, advanced manufacturing, advanced materials, and natural resources. IOF expects to invest in at least 15 Oregon companies, with substantial reserved investment capital to support follow-on investments in those companies that meet or exceed expectations.

Steve Eichenlaub and Angela Jackson, Managing Directors of Portland Seed Fund IV, are the Managing Directors of IOF, joined by Shashi Jain as Venture Partner, bringing his deep science and technology start-up experience to help source, vet, mentor, and advise IOF portfolio companies.

This fund runs based on an annual commitment over 4 years, and I am a passive LP here.

positions.title: Community Liaison
positions.description:
The Metro Region Innovation Hub received its initial funding from Business Oregon and aims to catalyze innovation and entrepreneurship across the region by connecting entrepreneurs with vital resources in networking, coaching, education, and capital access. The Hub supports entrepreneurs through personalized navigation, addressing gaps in existing resources, and fostering collaboration across regional partners. The Metro Region Innovation Hub serves entrepreneurs from Multnomah, Clackamas, and Washington Counties in Oregon.

The mission is to foster and grow innovative businesses by providing regional entrepreneurs from all sectors, backgrounds, and business stages with accessible paths to regional resources in networking, coaching, education, and capital access. We open up this accessibility through one-to-one guided navigation of existing regional resources and supporting programs that fill gaps in existing regional resources.

Key Objectives 
* Building and maintaining strong relationships with local entrepreneurs and community leaders within targeted underserved or under-resourced groups.
* Engaging and inviting entrepreneurs to participate in Hub programs and other relevant events in the community.
* Engaging entrepreneurs from the community and connecting them with the Hub’s Navigator Program, helping them access the resources and guidance they need to grow.
* Facilitating the participation of entrepreneurs from the community in Hub-specific programs, furthering their business development.
positions.insights: Skills: Bootstrap Startup · Sustainability · Fundraising · Climate Tech · Education Technology · Robotics · Artificial Intelligence (AI) · Entrepreneurship · Investing · Community Building · Software Development · Venture Capital · Benefit Companies · Start-ups · Communication

positions.title: Founder
positions.description:
I built Shiro to enable teams to automate test-driven prompt engineering practices for their large language model integrations. The platform enables teams to iterate on prompts, by performing automated tests and version control. These tests include both qualitative and more importantly quantitative data. Allowing teams to use data to compare variations on prompt language, parameters, models, and even model providers across a suite of test cases.

I developed the platform using Ruby and Python, integrating with all the major large language model providers including OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Anthropic, AWS, and Microsoft. A huge help with the heavy lifting was the Jumpstart Pro Rails template by Chris Oliver.

I created the tool to help businesses quickly optimize their internal AI processes during the rapidly evolving scramble to test, validate and implement the latest and greatest large language model versions.

In 2024 I sold Shiro, to pursue work on Rose City Robotics. I love the core technology I developed at Shiro and it was fun to sell the business to another entrepreneurial Ruby developer.

positions.title: Co-founder (exit)
positions.description:
What started as a class project at Babson turned into 17 years. I led teams across marketing, product development, software, accounting and customer service. I engaged and managed a diverse array of external professionals including instructors, lawyers, software developers, designers, analysts, and consultants. I demonstrated prudent financial management by strategically investing cash flows from operations to maximize business growth while minimizing risk.

After learning Ruby, I led our software development team, architecting and building our home-grown online learning management platform, providing millions of lessons to students all over the world. I exemplified core values of integrity, care, and empathy to ensure exceptional customer experiences. I established and maintained robust information systems for open financial transparency with employees, contractors, and partners. Also, I ran payroll, closed monthly books, directed AP/AR, and generated quarterly financial statements and budgets.

• Earned customer satisfaction rating of 4.6/5 by ensuring high-quality experiences for 100K community members across 200+ free and paid courses.
• Rode the solar coaster, decreasing annual OpEx once by 73% and again by 47% to maintain profitability by successfully steering two industry downturn cycles.
• Automated accounting systems to reduce repetitive work by 94% via automated and transparent vendor payment calculations and streamlined AP/AR system.
• Attracted, hired, and onboarded 11 employees and recruited and managed 40+ independent expert instructors and partners to develop content for the community.

In 2022 I sold HeatSpring and left the business. Very deeply important to me at HeatSpring was doing something every day that I felt good about, by spreading high-quality education honestly and transparently, for the benefit of the clean energy industry. When that was no longer possible, I decided to sell and start something new.

honors.title: Audience Award Winner
honors.description: For over two decades, BVC has stood as Central Oregon’s flagship entrepreneurship event. The program creates an opportunity to connect prominent investors and industry leaders with startup founders looking to scale. With separate categories for growth, early and new economy companies, BVC aims to garner as much exposure for participating startups as possible and serves as a catalyst for additional funding for the portfolio of companies that participate. The exposure and connections made at BVC are laying the foundation for the future of Central Oregon’s economy while connecting investors and promising startups from across the country to foster long-term relationships.
honors.issuer: Issued by Bend Venture Conference  · Oct 2024

honors.description: Early stage startup pitch competition, September 2024

volunteerExperiences.description: I mentor and coach a 7th and 8th grade FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) team for Bridger Creative Science School in Portland, Oregon. In 2026 our rookie robotics team "The Vikings" (go PSU) advanced to the playoffs at the FIRST Oregon Hillsboro Qualifying Tournament ranked #10 of 24 teams.

The Robotics Collaborative is a nonprofit organization based in Oregon, dedicated to advancing the next generation of robotics through mentorship and open community building. Founded by a team of engineers, educators, and STEM advocates, we are united by a shared FIRST Robotics belief in the next generation: building robots to build people. 

We support and grow a vibrant, hands-on robotics community by partnering with local schools, makerspaces, universities, corporations and research institutions. As part of our commitment to technical excellence and youth engagement, we actively support the activities of teams in FIRST Robotics FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC), a robotics competition for students in grades 7–12

We directly support FTC team #30603, a community team for grades 7–8 in Portland, Oregon and I serve as the head coach for this team, as well as the program director for the Robotics Collaborative.

FIRST Robotics is a global organization that inspires young people to become science and technology leaders through hands-on robotics programs.

experience.title: Founder
experience.description:
I built Shiro to enable teams to automate test-driven prompt engineering practices for their large language model integrations. The platform enables teams to iterate on prompts, by performing automated tests and version control. These tests include both qualitative and more importantly quantitative data. Allowing teams to use data to compare variations on prompt language, parameters, models, and even model providers across a suite of test cases.

I developed the platform using Ruby and Python, integrating with all the major large language model providers including OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Anthropic, AWS, and Microsoft. A huge help with the heavy lifting was the Jumpstart Pro Rails template by Chris Oliver.

I created the tool to help businesses quickly optimize their internal AI processes during the rapidly evolving scramble to test, validate and implement the latest and greatest large language model versions.

In 2024 I sold Shiro, to pursue work on Rose City Robotics. I love the core technology I developed at Shiro and it was fun to sell the business to another entrepreneurial Ruby developer.

volunteerExperience.description: I mentor and coach a 7th and 8th grade FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) team for Bridger Creative Science School in Portland, Oregon. In 2026 our rookie robotics team "The Vikings" (go PSU) advanced to the playoffs at the FIRST Oregon Hillsboro Qualifying Tournament ranked #10 of 24 teams.

The Robotics Collaborative is a nonprofit organization based in Oregon, dedicated to advancing the next generation of robotics through mentorship and open community building. Founded by a team of engineers, educators, and STEM advocates, we are united by a shared FIRST Robotics belief in the next generation: building robots to build people. 

We support and grow a vibrant, hands-on robotics community by partnering with local schools, makerspaces, universities, corporations and research institutions. As part of our commitment to technical excellence and youth engagement, we actively support the activities of teams in FIRST Robotics FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC), a robotics competition for students in grades 7–12

We directly support FTC team #30603, a community team for grades 7–8 in Portland, Oregon and I serve as the head coach for this team, as well as the program director for the Robotics Collaborative.

FIRST Robotics is a global organization that inspires young people to become science and technology leaders through hands-on robotics programs.
